Revisits
Get mock-control ready to publish as an Angular-only package pumice

The first revisit. It uses revisits:, which no format plan defines yet; one in aide will, from how this goes. Vellum pinned msw@2 inside a Chose: to get past a broken install step. That quietly re-decided something that belongs to pumice's ground, so this plan stands where pumice stood and asks the question properly.

Decision: What moved is our understanding, not the world

where projects/mock-control/README.md › mock-control › Requirements file page

quote - Angular 22, with MSW 2.

Because (measured): MSW 3.0.0 was published on 2026-09-28, a month before pumice. "MSW 2" was already stale when pumice wrote the README; the workspace happened to have 2.15. No pumice entry decided it, so this anchors where the assumption shows, not to an entry. That's a gap in pumice, found by revisiting it.

Decision: Ask it in pumice's frame: what's cheapest before the first publish

where plans/2026-10-29-pumice.md › Selectors use the library's prefix, `mock-panel`

entry Decision: Selectors use the library's prefix, mock-panel in pumice

Because (pumice, Jeff): pumice renamed the selectors because "a rename is cheapest before the first publish." A peer range is the same kind of promise: widening it later is easy, but publishing one that excludes npm's latest makes every new install fail the way vellum's did.

Decision: Measure both versions, the same three ways

where projects/mock-control/package.json › peerDependencies › msw file page

quote "msw": "^2.15.0"

Because (Claude, not asked): the library has no tests, so "works" has to be measured from outside. For MSW 2.15 and 3: the library builds against it; a fresh app following the README compiles; and in headless Chromium, a mocked endpoint answers with the mock and a pass-through endpoint is logged as passthrough. The pass-through check matters most: the library detects it by MSW's internal x-msw-intention header, which still exists in 3 but is the most likely thing to break quietly.

Decision: If both pass, support both; if 3 fails, stay on 2 and say why

Because (Claude, not asked): supporting both keeps the class apps working on 2 while a new install gets 3. The one known difference is the start option (onUnhandledRequest in 2, onUnhandledFrame in 3), which the README can say in a line. If 3 fails, the README explains the pin instead of just making it.

Decline: Re-measuring the known limits on MSW 3

where projects/mock-control/README.md › mock-control › Known limits (measured, msw 2.15, Chrome) file page

no quote, so nothing to search for

Because (Claude, not asked): client aborts and a long-hidden tab need real browser sessions, minutes long. The section's heading already says what it was measured on, so it stays true. Re-measuring is its own round if it matters.

Guess: The library works on MSW 3 unchanged

Answered in the as-built: held.

Disproved if: the library fails to build against 3, or either runtime check fails.
